sections.executive_summary:
OzMart’s warehouse integrates 137,901 order items through eleven native SSIS data flows. Five dimensions support customer, product, supplier, calendar and regional analysis. Original measures and statuses remain auditable; delivered orders define the completed-sales proxy. Source costs and universally missing freight prevent a reliable profit calculation.

Customer revenue leaders differ substantially across states: the leading exact ages range from 19 in ACT to 85 in Tasmania. Toys & Games leads delivered unit sales in all eight states, including 24,667 units in NSW. NSW-origin supplier Erin Marquez leads both 2022 and 2023 with 833 and 598 units. Dense ranking preserves ties, so the 2021 top-five-rank supplier result contains seven suppliers. These observations describe the supplied period and do not establish causal customer preferences or future demand.

Loan modelling uses 9,998 labelled records, an independent 80/20 split and training-only five-fold cross-validation. Logistic regression and a decision tree both miss every held-out default. Logistic regression has test AUC 0.625, compared with 0.500 for the tree, but accuracy around 89% conceals zero default recall. Neither model supports automatic lending. Future work needs verified temporal predictors, predeclared loss-sensitive evaluation and new independent validation, alongside privacy, fairness and human review controls.
sections.query_4_1: Revenue is SUM(LineAmount) for delivered items, grouped by customer destination state and exact source age. DENSE_RANK retains all age groups sharing the highest revenue (Microsoft, 2026). The result contains one winner per state: ACT 19, NSW 57, NT 71, QLD 40, SA 81, TAS 85, VIC 35 and WA 31. NSW age 57 contributes 44,167.3311 in the source currency. These are aggregate revenue profiles, not per-customer spending estimates; cohort size and purchase frequency may explain differences. No currency conversion or causal targeting effect is assumed.
sections.query_4_2: Product type means the product category, and best-selling means delivered units rather than revenue or distinct order lines. Ranking is partitioned by customer destination state; DENSE_RANK retains tied category positions. The actual output has five categories in each of eight states, with no included ties. Toys & Games ranks first everywhere: NSW contributes 24,667 units, VIC 17,914 and QLD 17,836. Revenue is shown as supporting context. The result supports category-level stock review, but does not reveal margins, inventory availability or future demand.
sections.query_4_3: NSW suppliers means suppliers whose own location is in NSW, consistent with the supplier-origin interpretation. Delivered quantity is grouped by purchase year and seller. The contradictory location marked UNK is excluded from an NSW-specific result. Michelle Wells leads 2021 with 23 units; Erin Marquez leads 2022 and 2023 with 833 and 598. DENSE_RANK includes five distinct quantity ranks, giving seven suppliers in 2021 and five in each later year. A separate customer-destination NSW sensitivity returns different suppliers and 21 rows overall, demonstrating that the geographical interpretation matters. The calendar groups represent the supplied observation period; they should not be assumed to be equally complete years.
